Definition: to be (causatively make) large (in various senses, as in body, mind, estate or honor, also in pride)
BiblicalUsage: Gadal means to be great, and to make great — and it is used for God, for kings, and for ordinary men. David prays that God's name may be magnified for ever in 1 Chronicles 17:24, and Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and wisdom in 1 Kings 10:23. Samuel tells Israel to consider how great things the LORD has done for them in 1 Samuel 12:24, and Rehoboam's young men boast that his little finger shall be thicker than his father's loins in 2 Chronicles 10:10.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe greatness is measured by whose name grows. David wanted God's name magnified, and Rehoboam's friends wanted his own finger thicker. I hold that the greatness that lasts is the greatness that points away from ourselves and toward God.
